difficulty_reason: The lemma defines, for a collection of presheaves of sets, the family of sieves whose morphism sets are unchanged after restricting along the morphism, and proves that this family is a topology, indeed the finest topology in which all the given presheaves are sheaves (statement lines 11330-11345). The proof is a complete argument: the family is written as an intersection of the families attached to the single presheaves, so the companion result on intersections reduces the statement to one presheaf (proof lines 11348-11363); the three axioms are then verified, the second one in detail by reduction along a covering sieve and sheaf-theoretic manipulations (proof lines 11366-11410); and the author leaves to the reader only the routine check that the constructed map is inverse to the displayed one (proof lines 11411-11412). The non-formal content is the verification of the second axiom. The claim is H2: a reduction followed by an axiom check.
